text:
Both failing specs miss by about 1% (undershoot 233 vs 230 mV, PSRR 63.5 vs 64 dB). Quiescent current has about 18 µA of headroom (33 vs 51 µA). The cheapest fix is to spend some of that headroom on loop bandwidth. A higher fixed tail current and a higher diff-pair gm/Id raise gm1, which raises the unity-gain frequency. That improves both PSRR at 1 kHz and undershoot recovery. A modestly higher `kfu` also helps both, but it costs phase margin, and ringing (6.6 of 10 mV) leaves only moderate room for that.

 "params": {"Itail0": 3.2e-6, "gmid_in": 20.0, "kfu": 0.5},
 "bounds": {"Itail0": [2e-6, 6e-6], "kfu": [0.35, 0.65], "gmid_in": [16.0, 24.0]}}
